title: Pauri 5, sound: thaapiaa na jaae
hook: thaapiaa na jaae keetaa na hoe

segments.voice: Yesterday, nadar, the gracious glance that opens the door. Your line was the early hour opens. Did the first two minutes of today go to quiet? Day one hundred seventy-one.

Four pauris down. Today we start a new stretch of Japji, pauris five to eight, and it opens with a line built from two short no's. People make things and set them in place all the time: a trophy in a cabinet, a photo on a shelf, a sign over a shop door. We make them, we put them in place, and there they stay. The fifth pauri begins by saying, twice, that the One can't be handled that way. And it says it in a line with a soft, rolling sound.
screen: `A NEW STRETCH: PAURIS 5 TO 8.` → `A TROPHY SET IN PLACE.` → `TWO SHORT NO'S.`

segments.voice: The opening line: thaapiaa na jaae, keetaa na hoe. Let's sound it. Thaapiaa: THAA-pi-aa. The th here isn't the English th in thin; it's a t with a puff of breath after it, like the t in top said firmly. Thaap means to set up, to install, to establish, the way an image is set on a pedestal. Na jaae: na, not; JAA-ay, can be. Keetaa: KEE-taa, made. Na hoe: na, not; HO-ay, is, becomes. So you can already hear it: cannot be installed, cannot be made. Two no's, balanced on either side of the line like the two pans of a scale. Then the next line: aape aap niranjan soe. AA-pay aap: himself, by himself. Ni-RUN-jun: stainless, unstained. So: He is Himself, by Himself, the stainless one. Listen to the rhythm of the whole opening: short phrases, each ending on a soft vowel, jaae, hoe, soe. It rocks gently, back and forth. Later in this pauri comes a refrain you'll hear again in the next one, guraa ik dehi bujhaaee. Guraa: Guru. Ik: one. Dehi bujhaaee: give understanding. It's read two ways: as a request, O Guru, give me this one understanding, or as thanks, the Guru has given this one understanding. We'll open what that one understanding is tomorrow. Today just notice that the pauri starts with two no's about what the One is not, and ends with a yes, one understanding, given by the Guru.
screen: `THAAP — TO SET UP, TO INSTALL.` · `TWO NO'S, LIKE A SCALE.` · `AAPE AAP NIRANJAN SOE.` · `GURAA IK DEHI BUJHAAEE.` · then, large: `PAURI FIVE.`

segments.voice: Say the first line with me, slowly, out loud if you can. Thaapiaa na jaae. Keetaa na hoe. Again, and let the breath puff lightly on the th. Thaapiaa na jaae. Keetaa na hoe. Now add the next line. Aape aap niranjan soe. Say all of it once more, softly, and feel it rock back and forth. Then sit, and let the quiet come. If you pray, you can rest in Waheguru. The bell holds the time.
screen: `ਥਾਪਿਆ ਨ ਜਾਇ ਕੀਤਾ ਨ ਹੋਇ ॥ ਆਪੇ ਆਪਿ ਨਿਰੰਜਨੁ ਸੋਇ ॥`

segments.voice: Niranjan. Stainless, unstained: the One who cannot be installed or made, thaapiaa na jaae, keetaa na hoe.
Your line: thaapiaa na jaae. Today, when you set something down in its place, your keys, a cup, a book, say the line quietly once. Day one hundred seventy-one.

howItsDone: The fifth pauri of Japji is recited each morning; its refrain, guraa ik dehi bujhaaee, about the one understanding the Guru gives, comes back at the end of the sixth pauri.

original.say: THAA-pi-aa na JAA-ay, KEE-taa na HO-ay
original.note: Gurmukhi: the opening of Japji's fifth pauri, Ang 2. ਥ is an aspirated t.

trapdoor: what you thought: a line about something that can't be done.
what it means: the One cannot be installed or made; He is Himself, by Himself, stainless.
what a scholar hears: thaapiaa uses the verb for installing an image on its seat; niranjan is from anjan, the black of collyrium: without a stain.

notes: Thaap as installing an image: common gloss. Confirm framing avoids disparaging image worship (the script only says 'the One can't be handled that way').
Niranjan from anjan (collyrium): common etymology. Confirm.
Refrain 'guraa ik dehi bujhaaee' in pauris 5 and 6: confirm.

Reviewer edit: the refrain is read both as a request ('O Guru, give me this one understanding') and as a statement ('the Guru has given this one understanding', as in Macauliffe). The teach now names both instead of presenting the request reading as settled; day 172 uses both. Confirm preferred framing.
The carry asks the learner to say 'cannot be installed' while passing a statue or framed photo. Check this cannot read as a jab at image worship in other traditions.
